title: Implement bounded filterable events signals logs and health read commands
acceptance_criteria: history_commands.py exposes run_history_command(name, args) -> int and add_history_arguments(parser, name), handling signals, evaluations, events, logs and health
Results default to 50 rows, never exceed 1000, and are filterable by account/scenario, symbol, strategy, since/until, type, outcome, rejection reason and correlation ids, as demonstrated by tests
History commands open SQLite read-only; a test asserts that a write attempt through their connection fails, and no broker or data-provider module is imported
logs output is capped by both line and byte limits and filterable by level and run_id/cycle_id/signal_id/intent_id/client_order_id
health reports OFFLINE with exit code 5 when the heartbeat age exceeds the configured threshold under an injected clock, and exit code 0 when all conditions are healthy
observability/metrics.py defines metrics and alert evaluators for every condition listed in the description, each producing a HealthIssue with severity, code and remediation command text
The redaction filter masks API keys, secrets and tokens and masks account identifiers to the last 4 characters; tests assert that the raw values are absent from the output
Structured log records include bound run_id, cycle_id, signal_id, intent_id and client_order_id when set
tests/unit/test_history_commands.py contains passing positive and negative tests and uses no network access or broker credentials
forbidden_changes: edit mike_trade/cli.py or other controls modules owned by task s.3
write to the database or mutate configuration from history or health commands
return unbounded result sets or stream logs without caps
log or print secrets, full account identifiers or raw unfiltered provider payloads
remove or rename existing public observability APIs
access broker credentials or create broker orders
run broad test suites or backtests
